text:
alex: noticing slow mem reclaim on Dedicated pool when handling long-context (40k-60k) requests. host kernels differ from hosted (we're on 6.1 vs hosted 5.15). memory climbs ~200MB/request over ~30min under steady replay.
maya: hmm; is this the same workload as the paging regression from last month? any KV cache pprof traces?
alex: different shape. last month was eviction churn from tiny TTLs. this looks like fragments accumulating in the KV slab: we see lots of partial page allocations but low swap activity. pasted a perf script output below.
ryan: paste the perf please. also which allocator? jemalloc or tcmalloc on Dedicated?
alex: jemalloc. perf snippet:
```
# perf report summary
samples: kv_alloc+kv_reclaim
60% kv_alloc: frequent 4k allocs, backing by new pagefaults
22% kv_reclaim: latency spikes when reclaim scheduled
10% migrate_pages: NUMA cross-node
```
No heavy swap, but high page fragmentation counters.
tess: could be the kernel hugepage fallback behavior. hosted nodes have hugepage premap enabled; Dedicated we turned it off for GPU isolation. That causes more 4k allocations and fragmentation under KV reuse. Also VPC on Private forces MTU 9000 in some clusters which affects NIC offload and maybe DMA bounce buffers.
maya: interesting. So hypothesis: kernel config + hugepage policy -> more small-page churn -> higher fragmentation -> GC/reclaim scheduling can't compact because jemalloc chunks pinned by GPU driver mmaps? Any traces of vm_operations or madvise patterns?
alex: yes: we see GPU driver mmap ranges flagged VM_IO and MADV_DONTNEED calls are rare. Reclaim thread tries to free but per-chunk arenas are still referenced by the runtime due to striping across tenants. Attached repro command:
```
# repro harness
./repro_run --model gpt-redwood-7b --context 50000 --qcache=true --threads=32 --trace=kvprof.out
```
ryan: can you share kvprof.out? I can run pmap + jemalloc stats against it.
alex: uploaded kvprof.out to the `/tmp/runs/217123` bucket.
infra-ci: deploy-bot: started nightly job to collect kernel vmstat and jemalloc stats on Dedicated-n9 pool (job id 217123-rc1).
maya: if fragmentation is the issue, short-term we can tune jemalloc to favor larger arenas/chunk size and increase decay time so background purging is more aggressive. medium-term we should standardize hugepage setting across hosted/dedicated/private or at least have a runtime kernel-config check that warns on mismatch.
ryan: propose steps:
1) Run jemalloc opt: MALLOC_CONF=oversize_threshold:1,lg_chunk:22,decay_time:10000 (test on one node)
2) Enable hugepage premap on one Dedicated node and rerun repro
3) On Private (on-prem) check GPU driver ABI for MAP_SHARED vs MAP_PRIVATE mapping flags

alex: did step 1 locally: chunk->4MB reduced fragmentation in microbench but end-to-end still sees gradual growth (now 50MB/request). Step 2 pending infra access.
tess: FYI Dedicated pool has constrained kernel upgrade cadence; can't flip hugepage globally without SLA. But we can run a node-level kernel param via sysctl for transparent hugepage defrag and see impact.
maya: also check batching heuristic: if we increase batching window by 10-20ms, KV reuse pattern changes (more prefix reuse) and that can reduce new allocations. Maybe the runtime's continuous batching produces strided KV placement that fragments less if batched more.
alex: good catch — microbenchmark: +15ms batching window reduced new page allocs by ~30% since more requests hit same KV frames. Will prod more.
ryan: I'll coordinate with infra to run the 3-step trial on a Dedicated node and a Private onprem host next Tue. If we see consistent gap with hosted, we'll add a kernel sanity check in the startup logs and a remediation doc for customers.
alex: thanks — also logging the pprof flamegraph link: https://internal/fg/217123/kvfrag.html (contains sample symbols)
infra-ci: deploy-bot: job 217123-rc1 finished: collected vmstat, jemalloc stats, perf.data. Artifacts at: https://ci/internal/artifacts/217123-rc1
maya: plan summary for the thread:
- short-term: jemalloc chunk + decay tuning, 15ms batching tweak (runtime flag)
- medium-term: node kernel param check + optional hugepage premap on dedicated
- long-term: startup kernel sanity check + docs + automated suggestion (Optimize) to recommend config for Dedicated vs Private

alex: assigning myself to validate runtime flag impact and prepare a quick PR for config-check log message.
ryan: i'll own the infra trial and collect comparison matrix (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with the following metrics: resident delta per 10k tokens, pagefaults/sec, fragmentation score (from jemalloc), and KV reuse hit rate.
maya: perfect. add a test to perf-regressions nightly that runs the repro for 1 hour with 50k context to catch regressions early.
alex: ack. I'll drop notes in the reproducibility doc and ping when PR up. :thumbsup:
